title: Letting a Hillside Grow Back
transcript:
On a hillside above a former grazing settlement, a restoration team is taking an unusual approach to tree planting: it is deliberately leaving some areas unplanted. The decision follows a survey showing that young native trees are already returning in places where livestock no longer disturb the ground. The team wants to learn where natural recovery can do part of the work.

The hillside is far from uniform. Near an existing woodland, birds carry seeds into patches of shrubs that protect emerging seedlings from strong sunlight. Farther away, dense grass covers the ground and few young trees appear. Planting every part of the slope at the same rate would ignore these differences and use scarce seedlings where they may not be needed.

Workers have therefore divided the site into several treatment areas. In some, they remove invasive plants and wait. In others, they plant small groups of native trees rather than evenly spaced rows. These groups are intended to create sheltered starting points from which vegetation may gradually spread. Regular photographs and marked survey plots will show whether that expectation is justified.

The project coordinator says the approach should not be confused with abandoning the site. Fences still need maintenance, invasive plants may return, and young growth must be checked after dry periods. Saving on planting does not eliminate the need for observation or care.

The team will compare survival, species variety and labour costs over several seasons. Counting the number of trees put into the ground would produce a quick headline, but it would not reveal whether a resilient woodland was developing. For this project, success means establishing a process of recovery that can continue after the initial funding ends, not simply completing a planting target.

questions.prompt: Why is the team leaving some parts of the hillside unplanted?
options: The land is legally required to remain bare.
All available seedlings belong to non-native species.
Young native trees are already returning naturally in some places.
The team intends to resume intensive grazing everywhere.
questions.answer: Young native trees are already returning naturally in some places.
questions.explanation: 调查显示部分区域已出现天然更新，团队希望利用自然恢复减少不必要栽种。

questions.prompt: What helps seedlings establish near the existing woodland?
options: Shrubs shelter seedlings and birds bring in seeds.
Workers replace all the soil each month.
Dense grass prevents every other plant from growing.
The nearby trees stop all rainfall from reaching the slope.
questions.answer: Shrubs shelter seedlings and birds bring in seeds.
questions.explanation: 鸟类带来种子，灌木为幼苗遮挡强烈日照，两者促进天然更新。

questions.prompt: What does the coordinator stress about the less intensive planting approach?
options: It requires no further visits once fences are installed.
It still requires monitoring and maintenance.
It guarantees that invasive plants will disappear.
It can be evaluated solely by the number of seedlings purchased.
questions.answer: It still requires monitoring and maintenance.
questions.explanation: 减少人工种植并非放弃管理，围栏、入侵植物和旱后幼苗仍需照护。

questions.prompt: What is the project’s intended measure of success?
options: Meeting a planting total as quickly as possible.
Making every treatment area look identical.
Removing all shrubs before funding ends.
Starting a recovery process that can continue beyond initial funding.
questions.answer: Starting a recovery process that can continue beyond initial funding.
questions.explanation: 项目目标是形成资金结束后仍可延续的恢复过程，而不只是完成种植数量。
